turns.text: quick q. how do admissions readers actually review a summer engineering program application, like what do they weigh in the short answers. its the state university summer engineering institute, due nov 15

Summer programs are usually reviewed in a lighter, faster pass than college admissions. Typically:

- Readers (staff, faculty, sometimes past participants) skim for fit: genuine interest in engineering, evidence you've acted on it, and whether you'd contribute to a cohort.
- Short answers are weighed for specificity. A concrete project, problem, or moment beats broad statements like 'I love solving problems.'
- Clarity and voice matter more than polish. Readers see hundreds, so a direct, honest answer stands out.
- Grades, course rigor, and any recommender input usually act as a threshold, not the deciding factor.
- Many programs also care about who gets access, so context about your school or opportunities can help.

If you paste your responses, I can tell you where they're specific and where they're generic.

I want to work on how salt marshes handle flooding. On my robotics team I lead the mechanical subteam. Last month our drivetrain kept failing and i realised I had been fixing it myself instead of letting teammates try their own ideas. Once I started asking for there suggestions, we found the problem in two days.
